description: BC finance entity sets per company (item and general ledger entries, aged receivables/payables, purchase credit memos with lines, customer/vendor payment journals with their payment lines): record counts, field names, that every allowlisted $select/filter field exists live and that BC accepts each set's whole $select allowlist. A set a company does not expose (404) is listed in finance_not_exposed: a reason-coded gap, never zero records. Counts, field names and error classes only; never a value. My Company (company_0, Production, bc_company_books.json ledgers.required_book) is the required book: its customerPaymentJournals and vendorPaymentJournals must be served with lines (finance_required; finance_required_unserved must be empty). The consolidation and distribution companies' journal_template_missing 400 are reason-coded expected gaps (finance_expected_gaps: reason, company index, book label, entity set, owner Ricardo, cause payment_journal_templates_missing), never served, never finance_errors.
notes: live-unverified until a live-check result exists (bc-finance-2). The allowlists are integrations/live_source_grammar.py BC_QUERY_SPECS from the BC API v2.0 resource reference: a name BC does not serve shows in select_allowlist_absent and makes select_accepted false (BC answers 400 to an unknown $select field): a real finding (drop the name), not a flake. agedAccountsReceivables/-Payables are keyed by customerId/vendorId (BC_RECORD_KEY_FIELD); has_etag false there is allowed (the capture versions such a row by its content digest). Payment journal lines are read by journalId (BC_LINE_PARENT_FIELD); a journal with no lines leaves lines.records_returned 0. finance_not_exposed lists 404s per company index (the Portal reports customer/vendor ledger entries 404 on this tenant, plx-customer-portal@790256c inbound.ts:248-268; none of those sets is probed here). The capture of the same sets is bc.capture_full (units not_exposed counted in units_not_exposed). Diagnosis fields are injected-transport tested (integrations/tests/test_bc_read_entities.py). finance_errors counts failed reads, header and lines alike, by design: a set's lines read that fails (payment lines of a journal) is one error like a failed header read, so a count from 7b5c3896 on is not comparable one to one with the earlier dailies, which counted header failures only. A set that answers 200 with an empty value is served (records_returned 0, has_etag null), never an error; a header 404 is finance_not_exposed, never an error. The dailies of 2026-10-07/08 reported finance_errors 4 without naming the failed reads, and no company or set is inferred from row positions: each failed read is one finance_entity_errors row (company index, entity set, part header or lines, error class, HTTP status, error-code class, detail token), recorded per row, so the next daily verdict names each failed read's company, set and typed status (integrations/tests/test_bc_read_probe_counts.py, injected-transport, as bc.case_entities). Cause of the 2026-10-07..10 dailies' finance_errors 4, inferred from the published results: the probe's own records name no set (they predate finance_entity_errors) and show only that the four were header reads, none a 404, stable over 13 runs. The bc.capture_full daily of the same run (afddbcd), whose units carry entity_set and reason side by side, failed customerPaymentJournals of companies 1 and 2 and vendorPaymentJournals of company 2 with reason source_refused (a first-page 400/401/403; 57-character labels, the length of 'SourceUnavailable: business-central GET returned HTTP <3 digits>', so no retry) and vendorPaymentJournals of company 1 with a transport failure, while company 0 served both: BC refuses the payment journal listings of companies 1 and 2. No live record yet names their status and BC code (the last bc.ledgers record, 2026-10-10 18:18Z daily, predates finance_refused), so the command lists no --expected-refusal: the next daily names each with company, set, status and BC code (finance_refused, expected false) and fails. An upstream refusal: a header read answered 400/401/403 with a BC JSON error code while another company served the same read in the run (the request is valid and authorized) is a finance_refused row named by company index, book (the pinned company's, null when unpinned), entity set, status and BC code. The refusals this check expects are data in its command, scoped by company: --expected-refusal <company book>:<entity set>:<BC error code>, repeatable, the book being the company's in integrations/bc_company_books.json, matched by GUID, never a company index (a position, not an identity); a company-less entry, an unknown book, set or code, or the catch-all other, fails the probe before any request. An expected one is reported (expected true) and not counted; any other, the same set and code refused by a company the command does not list included, is also a finance_entity_errors row, so the check fails at once (never blocked, no 24 h window, never host_misconfiguration). Add a refusal here only when a live record shows its book and BC code. A refusal with no BC error code (a proxy page) or of a set no company served stays a finance error. An empty set is served only when BC answered 200 with an empty value array: such a set has records_returned 0 and has_etag null and no failure; a failed read has no records_returned. One retry layer (bc_read.ProbeBackoff, SourceApi's): a GET that failed in transport or with 429/502/503/504 is sent again after 5 s and 15 s (at most 3 GETs per read, 60 s of pause per probe); a Retry-After up to 15 s is honoured, a longer one is not retried. unit_retries and unit_retry_sleep_seconds equal get_retries and retry_sleep_seconds (kept for the records). Wall cap: no read starts, and no GET is sent again, that could end (30 s per attempt) past 240 s, under this check's 300 s timeout; a read cut there, before it starts or because the wall alone refused one of its GETs a retry, is a finance_entity_errors row with detail wall_cap and stopped_reason is wall_cap (every spec running the probe has a timeout above the cap by more than one attempt, asserted by integrations/tests/test_bc_read_probe_counts.py). Injected-transport tested: integrations/tests/test_bc_read_probe_counts.py, integrations/tests/test_bc_read_retry.py. Cause of the four refusals: every bc.ledgers record from 2026-10-11 on (the newest, results/daily/db0fbf3f4edaaa729ca05de8a49fb394d03b4ae9.json, carries the run at main efdaddb, checked 2026-10-11T22:58:33Z) names customerPaymentJournals and vendorPaymentJournals of companies 1 and 2 refused with HTTP 400, BC code other (outside that run's vocabulary) and expected false, with no book and no message_class (the run predates both); why BC refuses is not known (a missing journal template is a guess). Each failed finance read names message_class, the BC error message classified by fixed patterns into live_source_guard.MESSAGE_CLASS_TOKENS (journal_template_missing, journal_batch_missing, number_series_missing, setup_missing, permission_denied, invalid_query, record_not_found, field_validation, unclassified; null without a message), never a copy of the message, which carries names and filter values; the code vocabulary also names BC platform codes (internal_record_not_found, application_dialog_exception ...). The class is diagnosis on every refusal row, never a verdict: its patterns are English guesses no live message has confirmed, so no class makes a refusal expected; setup_missing names journal or payment setup only (another setup table, a currency's, is record_not_found). Only an --expected-refusal entry (book, set, BC code) makes a refusal expected (expected true, message_class kept; the row field reason, which repeated expected, is gone). BC's own code: the record of 2026-10-13T12:57:54Z (main dd215e9) names the four as books consol and distribution, HTTP 400, code other with every BC code then listed in the vocabulary, message_class journal_template_missing. The vocabulary now also admits BC's platform code family <Category>_<Name> (category Application, Authentication, Authorization, BadRequest, Internal or Request; a name of letters only, so no number, id, space or quote passes) as its snake-case token, and every failed finance read names its request (bc_read.request_shape: entity path below the company with record keys dropped, query option names, $select, $filter and $orderby field names, never a value). The request is not the cause: the header read is $top=1 with no $select or $filter, the pinned $metadata (ontology/schema/generated/meta/bc_metadata.json) declares every allowlisted name of both journal sets (a read naming a field the pin lacks is never sent; the select check then reads select_error metadata_unsupported), and company 0 serves the same read; BC's API page sets the company's default Cash Receipts / Payments journal template when it opens (microsoft/ALAppExtensions Apps/W1/APIV2 APIV2CustPaymJournals / APIV2VendorPaymJournals OnOpenPage, Graph Mgt - Journal GetDefault...TemplateName), so the refusal is the company's configuration. No record yet shows a BC code inside the vocabulary (other is never an entry), so the command lists none and the next daily fails on these four, naming each one's book, BC code, message_class and request: add one entry per refusal that record shows, citing it. live-unverified (injected-transport tested: integrations/tests/test_bc_read_probe_counts.py). Unserved sets (daily d298b51: customerPaymentJournals and vendorPaymentJournals of companies 1 and 2 answered HTTP 400, BC code internal_data_not_found_filter, request $top=1 only, message_class journal_template_missing): the request is not at fault, so it is not changed. A header 400 whose BC code is in bc_read.UNSERVED_CODES, that no --expected-refusal entry lists and that another company served in the run, is a blocked_upstream part (cause relation_unavailable, part <book or company_<index>>:<entity set>), not a finance error: the check is blocked naming each, never a pass, and expect_blocked requires finance_errors 0 and finance_served at least 1 over the rest. Classified by the BC code at run time, not per entity: a 401/403, another 400 code (invalid filter, bad request) and a set refused in every company stay finance errors. The same daily's itemLedgerEntries of company 2 (no status, detail retried.urlerror) is a transport failure after the retry layer: still a finance error, no class change (recorded here, no code change). internal_record_not_found is not in UNSERVED_CODES: it is BC's generic record-missing code and no live record shows it for an unserved set, so it stays a finance error. The live evidence on file (daily d298b51) records the four journal parts with internal_data_not_found_filter only. Later ask bc-unserved-endpoints (lead-owned) carries the unserved sets.
